source: github.com/sandeepkapri/BankNifty-Data (MIT). Upstream provider not named by the repository.
trust: The 1-minute file is trusted BY ASSOCIATION: the same author's NIFTY minute file was compared bar-for-bar against our Kite pull (846,741 shared bars, max disagreement 0.65 points, zero bars over 1 point). Nothing else in the repository inherits that.
volume: ABSENT upstream. Written as an EMPTY field, never 0.
dedupe: 3694 duplicate (day, minute) rows dropped, first occurrence kept; 3 of them carried OHLC differing from their first copy. 85 sessions were affected, 81 of them in late 2023 at 45 repeated minutes each.
derivation: 5m/15m/60m/1d are RESAMPLED HERE from the deduped 1-minute file. Buckets anchor on EACH SESSION'S OWN FIRST BAR, not a fixed 09:15, because Muhurat sessions open in the evening. The vendor also ships 5m/15m/1h/2h/3h files; they stop in April 2024 while the minute file runs to April 2026, so resampling is both more current and internally consistent.

vendor_daily_pre2015.DO_NOT_CONCATENATE: This is a DIFFERENT SERIES from 1d/all.csv, not an earlier part of it. Over the 2,292 days where both exist the closes differ with median |diff| 19.25 points -- symmetric, no bias (median signed -0.60, 49% positive), and the vendor close is inside our intraday range on 100% of days. Two independent series. Splicing them makes a discontinuity at the join that nobody will ever find again.
vendor_daily_pre2015.ALSO: BankNifty launched in September 2003 with a base of 1000 on 2000-01-01, so everything before late 2003 is a BACK-COMPUTED index that never traded. And 1368 rows have O=H=L=C, i.e. close-only data with the close copied into all four fields: every high/low measure over that period reads a range of zero.
